ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The table lists the conditions of ecological bottles A and B. Bottle A is “+” in the “light” column, and bottle B is “−” in the “light” column; both bottles are “+” in each of the columns “sediment containing microorganisms,” “planktonic algae,” “aquatic plants,” and “zooplankton.” The stem states that both ecological bottles are sealed and transparent, and that after a period of time, the ecosystem of bottle A is more stable than that of bottle B. Reasoning: The key difference between bottle B and bottle A is that there is no light. Planktonic algae and aquatic plants are producers. When lacking light, they cannot normally carry out photosynthesis, and cannot continuously produce organic matter and release oxygen. In a sealed ecological bottle, food and oxygen will gradually become insufficient. Zooplankton, as consumers, will have their survival and reproduction inhibited. Therefore, after a period of time, the population density of zooplankton in bottle B will decrease.
